subject: sr-business-studies
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name any two factors included under demographic environment.
questions.answer: Size, density, distribution and growth rate of population (also age composition).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: A private company must write ______ at the end of its name; a public company must write ______.
Fill in the blanks: Planning is the ______ function of management and is ______ (looks ahead).

Fill in the blanks: (a) ______ is the process of telling people what to do and seeing that they do it in the best possible manner. (b) ______ refers to the process by which a person transmits information to another.
Match: (a) Job description (b) Job specification with (i) statement of duties and responsibilities (ii) qualifications, skills and abilities required.
State true or false: (i) Co-ordination leads to diversity in action. (ii) Control is a continuous process.
Fill in the blanks: (i) Capital structure includes ______ liabilities. (ii) Financial structure includes ______ liabilities and ______ liabilities.
Fill in the blanks: Loans from financial institutions are granted for a maximum period of ______ years, while commercial banks grant loans for ______ years.
Expand: (i) IPO (ii) FPO (iii) SEBI.
questions.answer: (i) Initial Public Offering. (ii) Follow-on Public Offering. (iii) Securities and Exchange Board of India.

questions.q: Which pricing method? (a) Hari fixes the price 10 per cent above cost. (b) A fruit seller raises mango prices in the season of heavy demand.
Name the sales promotion tool: 50 g extra in a 250 g pack of tea.
Match: (i) Bulk Breaking (ii) Bulk Buying with (a) Wholesaler (b) Retailer.
questions.answer: (i) Bulk breaking – (b) Retailer (buys in bulk and sells in small quantities); (ii) bulk buying – (a) Wholesaler.

questions.q: Name the document: (a) An agreement signed with the shipping company to put goods on the ship. (b) Issued by the captain of the ship after loading.
Give two examples of self-employment.
questions.answer: A person running a grocery shop and a person running a tailoring shop.

questions.q: Name any two e-commerce businesses.
questions.answer: Amazon and Flipkart (also eBay, Myntra, BigBasket).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State any two responsibilities of business towards the shareholders or owners.
questions.answer: To ensure safety of investment and to provide a fair and regular dividend (also information and capital appreciation).

questions.q: Distinguish between job description and job specification.
questions.answer: Job description states duties and responsibilities; job specification states the qualifications and skills required.

questions.q: Why is wealth maximisation superior to profit maximisation?
questions.answer: It considers risk and the time value of money and focuses on earnings per share, unlike vague profit maximisation.

questions.q: State any two needs for long-term finance.
questions.answer: To purchase fixed assets and for modernisation or mergers and acquisitions (also R&D).

questions.q: 'Buy one get one free'. Identify the marketing activity and state any three of its objectives.
questions.answer: Sales promotion. Objectives: to attract new customers, to increase sales in the short run and to introduce a new product (or clear stock).

questions.q: Define 'Letter of Credit'.
questions.answer: A document issued by the importer's bank in favour of the exporter assuring payment of the exporter's bill up to the specified amount.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the limitations of a joint stock company (any three).
questions.answer: Difficult to form, control by a group, excessive government control, delay in decisions and lack of secrecy.

questions.q: Explain the process of control in three steps (any three).
questions.answer: Setting standards, measuring actual performance and comparing it with standards.

questions.q: State the advantages of stock exchanges to investors.
questions.answer: Ready facility to buy and sell, safety of dealings, regular price information and loans from banks against securities.

questions.q: State any three objectives of sales promotion.
questions.answer: To attract new customers, to increase sales in the short run and to introduce a new product.

questions.q: What is a departmental store? Give any three features.
questions.answer: A large retail store selling a wide variety of goods in one building divided into departments under central management; each department sells specific goods; it provides facilities like home delivery and credit.

questions.q: State any three characteristics of small business.
questions.answer: Owner-managed, limited area of operation, uses local resources and flexible.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps in the process of planning.
questions.answer: Establishing objectives, making assumptions (premises), identifying alternatives, evaluating alternatives, selecting a course of action, implementing the plan, and review and follow-up.

questions.q: Explain any five factors affecting the working capital requirement of a business.
questions.answer: Nature of business, scale of operations, business cycle, seasonal factors, production cycle, credit policy, operating efficiency and inflation.

questions.q: Explain the components of the product mix.
questions.answer: Product characteristics, branding, packaging and labelling.

questions.q: What options are available for securing online transactions? Explain.
questions.answer: Passwords, authentication, encryption, digital signatures and trusted third parties, though stolen cards and fraudulent sites need vigilance.
